purpose: User-requested causal investigation of apparent8-writer gains and16-writer losses. Preserve the original buffer-reuse qualification failure; these instrumented diagnostics are excluded and cannot replace it. No additional engine optimization or adoption.
evidence_trigger: Third16-writer pair reaches577743/576255 puts/s with4.392/4.337ms p99, while another pair has only1.3% more syncs but57.5x marker latency.8-writer ratios reverse across rounds. Historical16 results also include wins.
instrumentation: LD_PRELOAD diagnostic shim forwards synchronous WAL pwrite64/fdatasync/fallocate calls directly to their Linux syscalls, timestamps calls and records marker coordinates. One bounded pre-touched in-memory event array is flushed only at process exit; no trace-file I/O during measured writes. Parent samples block counters, I/O pressure, child worker wait channels/syscalls and task CPU ticks at100ms, retaining samples in memory until child exits. No kernel settings, firmware, allocator or global tracing settings change.
observer_limits: Kernel syscall tracepoint access fails under current account. Sched_schedstats is0, so zero run-delay counters cannot establish absence of scheduling delays. No active NVMe hwmon/SMART polling during runs, because prior repo experiments identify polling as an interference source. Sampler/interposer perturbation makes all8 runs diagnostic only. I/O shim does not capture asynchronous DATA requests or all file metadata syscalls; block counters are whole-device and100ms sampling can miss short waits.
assessment: Report all8 fixed diagnostics, including slow calls, per-round/per-binary8vs16 effects, marker/sync counts and latency distributions, extent write/lock overlap, device busy time, task states and CPU placement. Do not filter stall states, retry scores, infer SSD firmware cause from host timing, or claim a fast-pair comparison proves uniform nonregression. Stop after this bounded diagnostic for review.
